html:
Mother Teresa was a Catholic nun of Albanian family, born in Skopje in 1910, who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta to care for the dying and the poor.

She joined the Sisters of Loreto at 18 and was sent to India in 1929, where she taught at a girls' school in Calcutta for nearly twenty years. In 1946 she felt called to serve the poorest directly. She left the convent, put on a white sari with a blue border and began work in the slums. In 1950 the church approved her new order, and in 1952 she opened a home for the dying at Kalighat.

The order spread to India's leper colonies and orphanages and then around the world. She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.

She was also criticised. Doctors who visited said her homes gave poor medical care and little pain relief, and writers such as Christopher Hitchens attacked her views and some of her donors. She died in Calcutta in 1997 and was made a saint by Pope Francis in 2016.
sum: Mother Teresa was a Catholic nun of Albanian family, born in Skopje in 1910, who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta to care for the dying and the poor.
